name: College of Marin - Undocumented and Special Populations
description: Undocumented (and Special Population) Student Services strives to create a supportive and welcoming environment for all students. Our goal is to provide students with the guidance, services and resources needed to be successful at the College of Marin. Support includes information and assistance with AB540, financial aid application, free immigration legal services and more.

name: Santa Rosa Junior College - IGNITE Program / Second Chance Program
description: Second Chance is committed to providing a judgment -free space for systems - impacted students to break the cycle of recidivism through education and empowerment. Regardless of how long you have been inside, or where you have been in the justice system (priso n, jail, juvenile hall, or probation camp), you will find a home on campus and a place of belonging in Second Chance.

name: Sonoma State University
description: Education services. Financial aid and tuition assistance available.

name: Behavioral Health Reintegration Program (BHR)

name: NAMI Marin County
description: Provide advocacy, education, support, and public awareness so that all individuals and families affected by mental health conditions in Marin County can build better lives.

name: Bay Area Community Resources
description: We deliver prevention, assessment, intervention, treatment and recovery support services to youth, families, and adults in our community. We also coordinate youth and community-led substance use advocacy and social change programs.

name: Marin Department of Health and Human Services
description: With over forty programs and eight hundred staff across twelve locations, Health and Human Services is the largest department within the County of Marin. At HHS our mission is to promote the health, well-being, self-sufficiency, and safety of all people in Marin County.
address: 20 N San Pedro Road, Suite 2028, San Rafael, CA

name: Catholic Charities of San Francisco – Homeless and Housing Services
description: Residential care facilities, distribution of housing subsidies and wrap-around case management provide people with freedom to focus on restoring housing stability and other areas of their lives.

name: Coordinated Entry System for Marin County
description: The purpose of Coordinated Entry is to ensure all people experiencing homelessness have fair and equal access to resources.

name: St. Vincent DePaul
description: Emergency assistance and housing counselors.
address: 820 B Street, Suite R., San Rafael, CA 94901

name: Ritter Center
description: Our vision is to compassionately establish healthy, housed community that has continual access to high-quality healthcare and support services regardless of the ability to pay. The Ritter Center prevents and resolves homelessness and improves the health, dignity and well-being of people living in poverty in Marin County by providing high-quality, culturally sensitive, easily accessible medical care and social services.

name: Bloom
description: The right clothing for an upcoming interview or new job removes barriers to self- sufficiency and keeps families intact. A two-week wardrobe tailored to everyone’s needs is provided, whether with overalls and work boots, or suits and ties. The new sense of self-worth and hope for our participants’ experience is transformational. Center Point

name: Community Action Marin
description: We break down barriers that get in the way of anyone in our community being able to support themselves, and each other. Our clients come to us because they have a need for one of our services. When community members come through any one of our doors, we put them first, listen to what they need and give them more than just the tools to meet the basic requirements for survival. Our bilingual and bicultural staff ensures that people are heard— from immediate needs to making long-lasting change a reality in support of equity and well- being for all.

name: Re-Entry Success Center
description: The experience of arrest, custody, and reentry into community is difficult. We believe that reentry planning and preparation should begin as early as possible after first contact with police and the courts. The Reentry Success center is the outcome of one community’s desire to create a different path to reentry. Thanks to them, the Reentry Success Center is firmly rooted in clear and honest core values. We offer hope, healing, and justice for justice-impacted people and their families. Working with a community of partners, we provide free, integrated and effective services in one welcoming hub.
